title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: Performance & Scalability
summary: Production RAG systems must meet strict latency SLAs — typically P95 < 2 seconds.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Production RAG systems must meet strict latency SLAs — typically P95 < 2 seconds. Latency decomposes into: **(1) retrieval latency** (ANN search, network to vector DB) + **(2) embedding latency** (encode query) + **(3) reranking latency** (cross-encoder inference) + **(4) LLM generation latency** (TTFT + token generation). The first three are optimizable to < 100ms. LLM generation is the dominant cost (500ms–3s). Strategies: parallel retrieval + pre-generation, semantic caching, streaming responses, and smaller models for simple queries.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
RAG LATENCY BREAKDOWN — WHERE TIME IS SPENT
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

BASELINE (Unoptimized):
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Query received
  │
  │  Query embedding: ────────── 80ms
  │  ANN search:      ─────── 60ms
  │  Reranking:       ──────────────── 120ms
  │  LLM generation:  ──────────────────────────────── 1800ms
  │                                                           
  ▼                                                           
Total P50: ~2060ms    P99: ~3200ms  ❌ Exceeds SLA

OPTIMIZED:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Query received
  │
  │  [CACHE CHECK + EMBEDDING in parallel]
  │  Cache check:     ── 5ms
  │  (20-40% of queries end here → ~10ms total)
  │
  │  Cache miss path:
  │  ANN search (quantized): ──── 30ms  (was 60ms, 2x faster)
  │  Reranking (skip if top score >0.95): ── 40ms (adaptive)
  │  LLM: fast model for simple queries
  │    GPT-4o-mini: ─────────── 400ms  (was 1800ms)
  │    GPT-4o:      ─────────────────────── 1200ms
  │
  ▼
P50: ~480ms (simple)  P99: ~1400ms (complex)  ✅ Meets SLA

OPTIMIZATION IMPACT TABLE:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Technique              Latency Saving    Complexity   Cost Impact
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Semantic caching       40-80% (on hits)  Low          Reduce API costs
Model routing          60-70% (fast)     Low          10x cheaper
ANN quantization       20-40% search     Medium       None
Adaptive reranking     30-60% (skips)    Low          None
Streaming response     Perceived -80%    Low          None
Chunk compression      20-30% tokens     Medium       Lower LLM cost

INGESTION SCALABILITY:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
10M Documents → How to ingest in 8 hours?

Calculation:
  Text-embedding-3-small: 1000 tokens/doc avg
  OpenAI rate limit: 10M tokens/min (Tier 4)
  Embedding rate: 10K docs/min
  Time needed: 10M / 10K = 1000 min = 16.7 hours (single worker)

  With 5 parallel workers: 1000 / 5 = 200 min ≈ 3.3 hours ✓

Architecture:
  Documents → S3
     │ trigger
     ▼
  Lambda/Worker Pod 1 ──┐
  Lambda/Worker Pod 2 ──┤ → Qdrant (batch upsert 200/request)
  Lambda/Worker Pod 3 ──┤
  Lambda/Worker Pod 4 ──┤ → Checkpoint (Redis or DynamoDB)
  Lambda/Worker Pod 5 ──┘
     
  Key: Idempotent workers (skip if doc_hash already processed)
       Crash-safe checkpoint (resume from last batch)
       Dead-letter queue for failed docs
```

options: Event-driven architecture: document source (S3 upload, API webhook, scraper) → message queue (Kafka/SQS) → embedding workers (horizontal scaling) → vector DB upsert.
Options: (1) Streaming: use llm.astream() + SSE (Server-Sent Events) to return tokens as they're generated — perceived latency drops dramatically; (2) Smaller model for…
Vertical: larger instance, more RAM (to fit more vectors in-memory) or more GPU VRAM (faster reranking inference).
Exact-match caching (Redis, Memcached) only hits when the exact query string appears again — effective for repeated identical queries.
quiz.explanation: Exact-match caching (Redis, Memcached) only hits when the exact query string appears again — effective for repeated identical queries. Semantic caching stores embeddings of past queries; when a new query arrives, compute its embedding and check similarity against cached queries — if cosine similarity > 0.95, return the cached answer.

quiz.question: What is product quantization and how does it speed up vector search?
options: Tier 1 (fastest, < 10ms): semantic cache lookup. Tier 2 (fast, < 100ms): ANN search in vector DB with quantized index.
Options: (1) Streaming: use llm.astream() + SSE (Server-Sent Events) to return tokens as they're generated — perceived latency drops dramatically; (2) Smaller model for…
Vertical: larger instance, more RAM (to fit more vectors in-memory) or more GPU VRAM (faster reranking inference).
PQ (Product Quantization) compresses float32 vectors (e.g., 1536 dims × 4 bytes = 6KB) by dividing into M sub-spaces and encoding each sub-space with a codebook of 256…
quiz.explanation: PQ (Product Quantization) compresses float32 vectors (e.g., 1536 dims × 4 bytes = 6KB) by dividing into M sub-spaces and encoding each sub-space with a codebook of 256 centroids (1 byte each). Result: 1536-dim vector → 96 bytes (16× compression). Distance computation uses lookup tables instead of full dot products — 10–50× faster.
